findings.title: Empty fingerprint acts as dedup key in appendToClosedJson, silently dropping multi-zero-fingerprint closures
findings.detail: In audit-runner.ts, appendToClosedJson and appendClosedRecordUnlocked deduplicate closed.json entries by fingerprint equality. When multiple findings have fingerprint='' (the default when no fingerprint is computed), only the first one is appended — all subsequent ones are silently dropped. The same issue exists in markFindingsClosed's in-memory dedup and closed.json write. Findings without fingerprints can never be tracked for regression detection anyway, but the data loss means closed.json does not reflect all closures.
findings.fix_sketch: Guard the fingerprint dedup check with a non-empty fingerprint condition: only skip appending if `record.fingerprint !== '' && alreadyRecorded`. Same fix needed in markFindingsClosed for both the in-memory alreadyQueued check and the existingFingerprints Set check.

findings.title: listActiveSprints in dashboard/server.ts fetches all sprint rows without a LIMIT
findings.detail: The SQL query in listActiveSprints uses ORDER BY updated_at DESC with no LIMIT clause, loading every sprint row from the state DB into memory at once. On a long-running deployment with thousands of completed sprints, this could load megabytes of data per request. The dashboard's /api/sprints/active endpoint then filters in JS, which means the unbounded DB read happens on every poll cycle regardless of how many active sprints exist.
findings.fix_sketch: Add LIMIT 500 (or a configurable cap) to the SQL query. Since the endpoint only shows active sprints (post-filter), 500 rows is a generous cap that covers any realistic active sprint count while bounding the query cost.
